questions.stem:
Figure 2 shows a sketch of a triangle $ABC$.
Given $\overrightarrow{AB}=2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}-2\mathbf{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}=5\mathbf{i}-6\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k}$,

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) find the size of angle $CAB$, giving your answer in degrees to 2 decimal places,
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
Attempts $\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\\-2\end{pmatrix}\cdot\begin{pmatrix}5\\-6\\1\end{pmatrix}=\sqrt{(2^2+3^2+(-2)^2)}\sqrt{(5^2+(-6)^2+1^2)}\cos(\angle CAB)$ M1
$\angle CAB=\arccos\left(-\frac{10}{\sqrt{17}\sqrt{62}}\right)=107.94^\circ$ dM1A1
M1: Attempts to use $\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}=|\mathbf{a}||\mathbf{b}|\cos\theta$ where $\mathbf{a}=\pm(2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}-2\mathbf{k})$, $\mathbf{b}=\pm(5\mathbf{i}-6\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k})$ i.e. correct use of Pythagoras to find and multiply the lengths together and multiplies and adds components (allow arithmetic slips) for dot product.
dM1: Dependent upon previous M1. For continuing to find $\angle CAB$ using invcos. Allow $\arccos\left(\frac{\pm 10}{\sqrt{17}\sqrt{62}}\right)$
A1: awrt $107.94^\circ$ only (Do not isw, so $107.94...$ followed by $180-107.94...=72.06...$ scores A0). Note that the correct answer in radians is $1.8839...$ and scores M1dM1A0 following correct work.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- dM1: Implied by previous M1 + angle rounding to $108^\circ$ or $72.1^\circ$ (NB $\cos\theta=-0.308…$)
- ALT (a): Calculates $|BC|=\sqrt{(5-2)^2+(-6-3)^2+(1--2)^2}$ M1; Uses cosine rule $\cos\angle CAB=\frac{17+62-99}{2\times\sqrt{17}\times\sqrt{62}}$ dM1; $\Rightarrow\angle CAB=\arccos\left(-\frac{20}{2\sqrt{17}\sqrt{62}}\right)=107.94^\circ$ A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) find the area of triangle $ABC$, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
Area $=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{17}\sqrt{62}\sin(107.94^\circ)=15.44$ M1A1
M1: Uses Area$=\frac{1}{2}|\mathbf{a}||\mathbf{b}|\sin C$ with $\mathbf{a}=2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}-2\mathbf{k}$, $\mathbf{b}=5\mathbf{i}-6\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k}$ and $C=$ their $107.94^\circ$
A1: Area = awrt 15.44 (Allow if $72.06^\circ$ is used for angle CAB)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- ALT (b): Area $=\sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}=\sqrt{\left(\frac{\sqrt{17}+\sqrt{62}+\sqrt{99}}{2}\right)\left(\frac{\sqrt{17}-\sqrt{62}+\sqrt{99}}{2}\right)\left(\frac{\sqrt{17}+\sqrt{62}-\sqrt{99}}{2}\right)\left(\frac{\sqrt{62}+\sqrt{99}-\sqrt{17}}{2}\right)}$ M1A1
- Alt (b) ii: Area $=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{|AB|^2|AC|^2-(\overrightarrow{AB}.\overrightarrow{AC})^2}=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{17\times62-100}=\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{106}$ M1A1
- ALT (b): Area $=\frac{1}{2}|a\times b|=\frac{1}{2}\begin{vmatrix}i&j&k\\2&3&-2\\5&-6&1\end{vmatrix}=\frac{1}{2}|-9i-12j-27k|=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{9^2+12^2+27^2}=15.44$ M1A1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Using your answer to part (b), or otherwise,
(c) find the shortest distance from $A$ to $BC$, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
Calculates $|BC|=\sqrt{(5-2)^2+(-6-3)^2+(1--2)^2}$ M1
Uses Area$=\frac{1}{2}|BC|\times|AD|\Rightarrow 15.44=\frac{1}{2}\times\sqrt{99}\times|AD|\Rightarrow |AD|=3.10$ M1A1
M1: Attempts to find the length of BC or BC$^2$ e.g. $|BC|=\sqrt{(5-2)^2+(-6-3)^2+(1--2)^2}$. Alternatively uses the cosine rule $BC^2=17+62-2\sqrt{17}\sqrt{62}\cos 107.9$. This may be seen in (a) or (b) but must be used in (c) to score this mark.
M1: Attempts to use Area$=\frac{1}{2}|BC|\times|AD|$ using their area from (b) and their $|BC|$. This may be implied by their working.
A1: $|AD|=$ awrt 3.10 (Not 3.1). Note that assuming AD bisects BAC without finding BC generally scores no marks.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- ALT (c): Calculates $|BC|=\sqrt{(5-2)^2+(-6-3)^2+(1--2)^2}$ M1; $\frac{\sin("107.94")}{BC}=\frac{\sin B}{"\sqrt{62}"}\Rightarrow B=48.84...\Rightarrow AD="\sqrt{17}"\sin B=3.10$ M1A1
- NB $BC=\sqrt{99}$ or $3\sqrt{11}$

questions.notes: [fix_parts] (c) mark_scheme: 'NB BC = √99 or 3√11' -> 'NB $BC=\\sqrt{99}$ or $3\\sqrt{11}$' (LaTeX for the completeness-pass line)

(2)

(c) find the shortest distance from $A$ to $BC$, giving your answer to 2 decimal places.
(3)
